subject: physics
question_text: What are the different types of errors that can occur in a measurement?

verification.note: Unit 2 has NO Short Answer or Long Answer section in EITHER source book — the Fastrack (pp.4-5) and the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.2-3) both list Very Short Answer questions only. So every Unit 2 card is a 2-mark VSAQ and no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. SOURCE DISAGREEMENT, recorded not resolved: the Fastrack (p.4) lists THREE types — systematic, random and gross. The TSBIE BLM (p.2) lists TWO — systematic and random. This card writes the Fastrack’s three and records the BLM’s two in the step’s why line.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Name the types
lines: Errors in a measurement are of three types:
steps.why: The Fastrack lists three. The TSBIE Basic Learning Material lists only systematic and random, treating gross errors as mistakes by the observer. Write all three; systematic and random are the two both books agree on.
common_mistakes: Listing only one type when the question says "types", which is plural.
Writing "least count error" as a fourth type. It is one kind of systematic error.

recall.must_convey: That the types are systematic, random and gross errors.

steps.memory_tip: Three types: systematic, random, gross. Systematic and random are the two both books list.
steps.margin_note: Number them. A numbered list reads as three separate points.

steps.label: What each one is

lines.text: Systematic errors repeat in the same direction

lines: Random errors vary in size and sign from
Gross errors come from the observer, such
as reading or recording a value wrongly.
steps.why: The difference is direction. A systematic error pushes every reading the same way, so averaging never removes it; a random error changes sign, so averaging does reduce it.
common_mistakes: Saying random errors can be removed by taking a better instrument. Averaging reduces them; a better instrument does not.

recall.must_convey: That systematic errors repeat in one direction, random errors vary, and gross errors are the observer’s.

steps.memory_tip: Systematic pushes ONE way every time. Random changes direction, so averaging shrinks it.
steps.margin_note: One line for each type is enough at 2 marks.

insider_note: The two source books disagree on the count. Write the three the Fastrack lists; naming systematic and random first is what earns the marks.
